text:
elena: quick thread: we've been reactive-demoting slabs on short prefetch spikes and it's causing read-amplification for tail cursors. proposal: try a short-lived 'backpressure window' that rate-limits prefetch admission for a prefix instead of moving credits immediately. thoughts?

matt: more context: when prefetch storms happen we see a cascade: prefetches evict hot prefix pages -> long cursors miss -> we prefetch again -> spirals. a local admission cap could break the loop.

rajesh: implementation idea: each prefix gets a token-bucket for prefetch admission. on spike we drop tokens instead of changing credit accounting. tokens refill slowly (configurable). cheaper and reversible.

ivy: important: token-bucket must be tenant-aware. don't penalize other tenants on same slab. per-prefix+tenant bucket? memory cost could explode.

elena: agree. we can shard the buckets: only create buckets for prefixes that exceed a cheap hotness threshold. ephemeral buckets GC after quiet period.

matt: what about correctness if a bucket denies prefetch and the request expects low-latency? we should fallback to on-demand fetch path (slower) but avoid evict choreography. caller gets a "prefetch_denied" hint so higher layers can adjust backoff.

rajesh: metrics to add: prefetch_denied_count, bucket_active_count, time_to_gc. also track downstream "raww_retry" (read-after-write retries) to ensure we don't increase RAWR.

ivy: rollout: feature flag off by default, enable in staging with synthetic prefetch storms. Canary 1% slabs with full telemetry. Ops kill-switch to disable quickly.

elena: micro-pseudocode:
```
if prefix.hotness > HOT_THRESHOLD and bucket.has_tokens():
  allow_prefetch();
else:
  deny_prefetch(); // fallback to sync readpath + backoff hint
```

matt: one more tradeoff: tokens vs credits. tokens don't change long-term fairness accounting. we need to ensure that prolonged denial doesn't starve tenant fairness allocations. add a leakage meter that converts long-term denied prefetch volume into credit compensation later.

rajesh: good point. emit "denied_to_compensate" events that reconciler consumes to top-up credits when cluster underutilized.

ops-bot: alert candidate: "prefetch_token_bucket_pressure" (p2) if denied_rate > 5% and rawr_retry_rate increased.

elena: thanks all. I'll write a short RFC with bucket lifecycle, GC heuristics, compensation events, and exact metrics. will ping SRE and product for acceptance criteria. :sparkles:
